title_en: Foreign Trade Law of the People's Republic of China

articles.content_en: Article 1 This Law is enacted in accordance with the Constitution for the purposes of advancing high-level opening up, promoting high-quality development of foreign trade, maintaining the order of foreign trade, protecting the legitimate rights and interests of foreign trade operators, facilitating the healthy development of the socialist market economy, and safeguarding national sovereignty, security, and development interests.

Article 2 This Law shall apply to foreign trade and the protection of intellectual property rights related to foreign trade.
For the purposes of this Law, "foreign trade" means the import and export of goods, the import and export of technologies, and international trade in services.
Article 3 Foreign trade work shall adhere to serving the national economic and social development and promoting the building of a strong trading nation.
Article 4 The competent department of foreign trade under the State Council shall, in accordance with this Law, be in charge of the national foreign trade work.
Article 5 The State shall implement a unified system of foreign trade, encourage the development of foreign trade, and maintain a fair and free order of foreign trade.

Article 6 The State shall actively align itself with international high-standard economic and trade rules, participate actively in the formulation of international economic and trade rules, uphold the multilateral trading system and a fair and equitable international economic and trade order, expand the network of high-standard free trade zones, optimize the environment for opening up and cooperation, and promote the building of an open world economy.

Article 7 The State shall establish a trade policy compliance mechanism aligned with internationally prevailing rules.
When formulating policies and measures concerning foreign trade, intellectual property rights related to foreign trade, and other aspects, the departments of the State Council, local people's governments at or above the county level and their departments shall carry out a trade policy compliance assessment in accordance with the relevant provisions of the State.

Article 8 The People's Republic of China shall, in accordance with the principle of equality and mutual benefit, promote and develop trade relations with other countries and regions, conclude or accede to regional economic and trade agreements such as customs union agreements and free trade zone agreements, and participate in regional economic organizations.

Article 9 The People's Republic of China shall, in respect of foreign trade, grant most-favored-nation treatment, national treatment, and other treatments to other contracting parties or participants in accordance with the international treaties and agreements it has concluded or acceded to, or grant most-favored-nation treatment, national treatment, and other treatments to the other party on the basis of the principle of reciprocity and mutual benefit.

Article 10 If any country or region takes discriminatory prohibitions, restrictions, or other similar measures against the People's Republic of China in respect of trade, the People's Republic of China may, according to the actual circumstances, take corresponding measures against such country or region.

Article 11 For the purposes of this Law, "foreign trade operator" means an individual or organization that, having undergone business entity registration or other practice procedures according to law, engages in foreign trade activities in accordance with the provisions of this Law and other relevant laws and administrative regulations.

Article 12 To engage in overseas labor service cooperation, an operator shall obtain the qualification for overseas labor service cooperation according to law. The specific measures shall be prescribed by the State Council.
To engage in overseas contracted projects, the operator shall file records in accordance with the relevant provisions of the State; if approval is required by laws or administrative regulations, the relevant provisions shall be followed.

Article 13 The State may implement state trading administration for the import and export of certain goods. The import and export of goods subject to state trading administration may only be conducted by authorized enterprises, except that the State may allow non-authorized enterprises to handle the import and export of a certain quantity of such goods.
The catalogue of goods subject to state trading administration and the list of authorized enterprises shall be formulated, adjusted, and published by the competent department of foreign trade under the State Council jointly with other relevant departments under the State Council.
If anyone, in violation of the provisions of the first paragraph of this Article, imports or exports goods subject to state trading administration without authorization, the Customs shall not release the goods.
Article 14 A foreign trade operator may, upon the commission of another party, handle foreign trade business on behalf of the commissioning party within its business scope.

Article 15 A foreign trade operator shall, in accordance with the provisions made by the competent department of foreign trade under the State Council or other relevant departments under the State Council according to law, submit to the relevant departments documents and materials related to its foreign trade business activities. The relevant departments shall keep the trade secrets provided by the operator confidential.
Article 16 The State shall permit the free import and export of goods and technologies, except where otherwise provided by laws or administrative regulations.

Article 17 The competent department of foreign trade under the State Council may, based on the need to monitor import and export conditions, implement automatic import and export licensing for certain goods that are freely importable and exportable and publish their catalogue.
For goods subject to automatic licensing, if the consignee or consignor submits an application for automatic license before going through the Customs declaration procedures, the competent department of foreign trade under the State Council or the institution entrusted by it shall grant the license; the Customs shall, upon presentation of the submitted automatic license certificate, handle the release procedures.
For the import or export of technologies that are freely importable and exportable, the contract shall be registered with the competent department of foreign trade under the State Council or the institution entrusted by it.

Article 19 The State may take any necessary measures to safeguard national security in respect of the import and export of goods and technologies related to fissionable or fusionable materials or materials derived therefrom, and in respect of the import and export related to weapons, ammunition, or other military supplies.
In time of war or other emergency situations in international relations, or for the maintenance of international peace and security, the State may take any necessary measures in respect of the import and export of goods and technologies.

Article 20 The competent department of foreign trade under the State Council shall, jointly with other relevant departments under the State Council, formulate, adjust, and publish catalogues of goods and technologies the import or export of which is prohibited or restricted, in accordance with the provisions of Articles 18 and 19 of this Law.
The competent department of foreign trade under the State Council, or it jointly with other relevant departments under the State Council, may, upon approval by the State Council, temporarily decide to prohibit or restrict the import or export of specific goods or technologies not included in the catalogues prescribed in the preceding paragraph, within the scope provided for in Articles 18 and 19 of this Law.

Article 21 The State shall implement quota, licensing and other forms of administration for goods whose import or export is restricted; it shall implement licensing administration for technologies whose import or export is restricted.
Goods and technologies subject to quota or licensing administration shall be imported or exported only with the permission of the competent foreign trade department of the State Council or the department jointly with other relevant departments of the State Council in accordance with the provisions of the State Council.
The State may implement tariff quota administration for some imported or exported goods.

Article 22 The import and export goods quotas and tariff quotas shall be allocated by the competent foreign trade department of the State Council or other relevant departments of the State Council within their respective scopes of duties in accordance with the principles of openness, fairness, impartiality and efficiency. The specific measures shall be prescribed by the State Council.

Article 23 Foreign trade dealers may conduct processing trade in accordance with law, importing all or part of the materials, and re-exporting the finished products after processing, assembling or repairing.
Where the State has prohibitive or restrictive provisions on processing trade goods, foreign trade dealers shall abide by them. The competent foreign trade department of the State Council shall, jointly with other relevant departments of the State Council, formulate, adjust and publish the catalogue of goods prohibited or restricted for processing trade.
Where the imported materials or finished products of processing trade cannot be re-exported, they may be sold domestically in accordance with law. Where the imported materials or finished products of processing trade that are sold domestically are subject to quota, licensing or tariff quota administration, a quota certificate, license or tariff quota certificate shall be obtained.

Article 24 The State shall implement a uniform commodity conformity assessment system. The certification, inspection and quarantine of imported and exported goods shall be conducted in accordance with the provisions of relevant laws and administrative regulations.

Article 25 The State shall implement rules of origin management for imported and exported goods. The specific determination of the origin of imported and exported goods shall be carried out in accordance with relevant laws and the provisions of the State Council and its relevant departments.

Article 26 Where other laws and administrative regulations have prohibitive or restrictive provisions on the import or export of cultural relics, wild animals, plants and their products, etc., such provisions shall be followed.

Article 27 The State shall encourage the development of international service trade in various modes, including cross-border supply, consumption abroad, commercial presence and movement of natural persons.

Article 28 The competent foreign trade department of the State Council and other relevant departments of the State Council shall administer international service trade in accordance with this Law and other relevant laws and administrative regulations.

Article 30 The State may take any necessary measures to safeguard national security with respect to international service trade related to the military, and international service trade related to fissionable or fusionable materials or materials from which such materials are derived.
In time of war or other emergencies in international relations, or for the purpose of maintaining international peace and security, the State may take any necessary measures in respect of international service trade.

Article 31 The State shall implement a negative list management system for cross-border service trade for foreign service suppliers conducting international service trade through cross-border supply, consumption abroad and movement of natural persons (hereinafter collectively referred to as cross-border service trade).
The competent foreign trade department of the State Council shall, jointly with other relevant departments of the State Council, formulate, adjust and publish the negative list for cross-border service trade.
Where foreign service suppliers conduct international service trade through commercial presence, they shall comply with the provisions of the Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China and other relevant laws and administrative regulations.
Where the international treaties or agreements concluded or acceded to by the People's Republic of China provide more favorable treatments for the conduct of international service trade, such provisions may be followed.

Article 32 The State shall strengthen the protection of intellectual property rights related to foreign trade, and protect intellectual property rights related to foreign trade in accordance with the laws and administrative regulations on intellectual property.
Where imported goods infringe upon intellectual property rights and endanger the order of foreign trade, the competent foreign trade department of the State Council may take measures such as prohibiting the import of the relevant goods produced or sold by the infringer within a certain period of time.

Article 33 The State shall conduct international exchanges and cooperation on intellectual property rights related to foreign trade, actively advance external negotiations on intellectual property rights related to foreign trade, establish and improve an overseas intellectual property early warning and rights protection assistance information platform, and enhance the intellectual property compliance level and risk response capability of foreign trade dealers.

Article 34 Where an intellectual property right holder engages in acts such as preventing a licensee from challenging the validity of the intellectual property right in the license contract, imposing mandatory package licensing, or stipulating exclusive grant-back conditions in the license contract, and such acts endanger the fair competition order in foreign trade, the competent foreign trade department of the State Council may take necessary measures to eliminate the harm.

Article 35 Where any other country or region fails to grant national treatment to individuals or organizations of the People's Republic of China in respect of intellectual property protection, or fails to provide sufficient and effective intellectual property protection for goods, technologies or services originating from the People's Republic of China, the competent foreign trade department of the State Council may, in accordance with the provisions of this Law and other relevant laws and administrative regulations, and based on the international treaties or agreements concluded or acceded to by the People's Republic of China, take necessary measures against the foreign trade with such country or region.

Article 36 In foreign trade activities, no monopolistic or unfair competition acts shall be committed in violation of the provisions of the laws and administrative regulations on anti-monopoly and anti-unfair competition.
Where monopolistic or unfair competition acts are committed in foreign trade activities and endanger fair market competition, they shall be dealt with in accordance with the provisions of the relevant laws and administrative regulations on anti-monopoly and anti-unfair competition.

Article 38 Foreign trade dealers shall, in foreign trade activities, comply with the relevant provisions on customs supervision and administration, foreign exchange administration, data security protection, etc.

Article 39 Where any violation of the provisions of this Law endangers the order of foreign trade, the competent foreign trade department of the State Council may make a public announcement and take necessary measures to eliminate the harm.

Article 42 The initiation of a foreign trade investigation shall be announced by the competent department of foreign trade under the State Council.
The investigation may be conducted by means of written questionnaires, hearings, on-site investigations, commissioned investigations, etc.
The competent department of foreign trade under the State Council shall, based on the investigation results, submit an investigation report or make a handling decision, and issue an announcement.

Article 43 Relevant individuals and organizations shall cooperate and assist in the foreign trade investigation.
The competent department of foreign trade under the State Council, other relevant departments under the State Council, and their staff members shall not disclose or illegally provide to others the state secrets, work secrets, trade secrets, personal privacy, and personal information learned during the foreign trade investigation.
Article 44 The State may, based on the results of the foreign trade investigation, take appropriate foreign trade remedy measures.

Article 45 Where products of any other country or region are imported into the Chinese market by way of dumping at a price lower than their normal value, causing material injury or threat of material injury to an established domestic industry, or materially retarding the establishment of a domestic industry, the State may take anti-dumping measures to eliminate or alleviate such injury, threat of injury, or retardation.

Article 46 Where products of any other country or region are exported to a third country market at a price lower than their normal value, causing material injury or threat of material injury to an established domestic industry, or materially retarding the establishment of a domestic industry, the competent department of foreign trade under the State Council may, upon application by the domestic industry, consult with the government of such third country and request it to take appropriate measures.

Article 47 Where imported products directly or indirectly receive any form of specific subsidy granted by the exporting country or region, causing material injury or threat of material injury to an established domestic industry, or materially retarding the establishment of a domestic industry, the State may take countervailing measures to eliminate or alleviate such injury, threat of injury, or retardation.

Article 48 Where a sharp increase in the quantity of imported products causes serious injury or threat of serious injury to a domestic industry producing like products or directly competitive products, the State may take necessary safeguard measures to eliminate or alleviate such injury or threat of injury, and may provide necessary support to such industry.

Article 49 Where an increase in the services provided by service suppliers of any other country or region to China causes injury or threat of injury to a domestic industry providing like services or directly competitive services, the State may take necessary relief measures to eliminate or alleviate such injury or threat of injury.

Article 50 Where a sharp increase in the quantity of a certain product entering the Chinese market due to restriction on imports by a third country causes injury or threat of injury to an established domestic industry, or retards the establishment of a domestic industry, the State may take necessary relief measures to restrict the import of such product.

Article 51 Where any country or region that has concluded or jointly acceded to an economic and trade treaty or agreement with the People's Republic of China violates the provisions of such treaty or agreement, thereby causing the loss or impairment of the interests that the People's Republic of China enjoys under such treaty or agreement, or obstructing the realization of the objectives of such treaty or agreement, the government of the People's Republic of China shall have the right to request the government of the relevant country or region to terminate such acts and take appropriate remedial measures, and may, in accordance with the relevant treaty or agreement, suspend or terminate the performance of relevant obligations.
Where the dispute settlement mechanism provided for in the relevant treaty or agreement cannot function normally, thereby causing the loss or impairment of the interests that the People's Republic of China enjoys under such treaty or agreement, or making it impossible to realize the objectives of such treaty or agreement, the government of the People's Republic of China may, in light of the actual circumstances, take corresponding measures.

Article 52 The competent department of foreign trade under the State Council shall, in accordance with the provisions of this Law and other relevant laws, conduct bilateral or multilateral consultations, negotiations, and dispute settlement work concerning foreign trade.

Article 53 The competent department of foreign trade under the State Council and other relevant departments under the State Council shall establish and improve an early warning and emergency response mechanism for import and export of goods, import and export of technologies, and international service trade, to address sudden and abnormal situations in foreign trade and safeguard national economic security.
The competent department of foreign trade under the State Council shall, as necessary, conduct trade policy evaluations of relevant countries or regions.

Article 54 The State may take necessary anti-circumvention measures, including adjusting the foreign trade remedy measures prescribed in Articles 45 to 51 of this Law, against acts that circumvent the foreign trade remedy measures prescribed in this Law.

Article 55 To address the impact of trade risks and changes in the trade environment, the relevant people's government may, as necessary, establish a trade adjustment assistance system that complies with the rules of the World Trade Organization, etc., and actively carry out trade adjustment assistance work to stabilize industrial and supply chains.

Article 56 The State shall formulate a foreign trade development strategy, promote balanced development of foreign trade, establish and improve foreign trade promotion mechanisms, and strengthen coordination between trade policies and fiscal, tax, financial, industrial and other policies.

Article 57 The State shall, in accordance with the needs of foreign trade development, establish and improve financial institutions serving foreign trade, improve insurance and safeguard measures, and promote the construction of a cross-border financial service system.
Article 58 The State shall develop foreign trade by means of import and export credit, export credit insurance, export tax rebates, and other ways of promoting foreign trade.

Article 59 The State shall support and promote the innovative development of foreign trade business forms and models such as cross-border e-commerce and comprehensive foreign trade services. The competent department of foreign trade under the State Council shall, in conjunction with other relevant departments under the State Council, establish and improve policy measures and management systems that meet the development needs of new foreign trade business forms and models.

Article 60 The State shall support the digital development of foreign trade, promote and strengthen the application of information technology means in foreign trade activities, support the use of electronic bills of lading, electronic invoices, etc., promote international mutual recognition of digital certificates, electronic signatures, etc., and enhance the level of digitalization and facilitation of foreign trade.
The State shall support and encourage the development of digital trade, establish and improve the digital trade governance system, improve digital trade regulatory measures, and promote the innovative development of digital trade.

Article 61 The State shall accelerate the establishment of a green trade system, encourage the import and export of green and low-carbon products, promote the construction of a system of product standards, certification, and labeling related to green trade, and strengthen international cooperation on green trade.
Article 62 The State shall establish a public information service system for foreign trade, providing information services to foreign trade operators and other members of the public.

Article 63 The State shall encourage foreign trade operators to explore international markets, guide and assist them in preventing and responding to risks, and develop foreign trade through various forms such as outbound investment, foreign labor service cooperation, and foreign contracting projects.
The State shall encourage professional service institutions such as finance, law, accounting, and intellectual property protection to improve their service networks, providing high-quality professional services for foreign trade operators to explore international markets, conduct business, respond to risks, and protect their rights and interests.

Article 64 The State shall support trade promotion platforms in enhancing their functions and service levels, assisting foreign trade operators in conducting foreign trade through domestic and international exhibitions, online trade platforms, and other means.
The State shall support and promote the construction of diversified and resilient international transport corridor systems, and improve foreign trade logistics services.

Article 65 Foreign trade operators may, according to law, establish and join relevant associations and chambers of commerce.
The relevant associations and chambers of commerce shall abide by laws and administrative regulations, provide their members with services related to production, marketing, information, and training in foreign trade in accordance with their articles of association, play a coordinating and self-disciplinary role, file applications for foreign trade remedy measures according to law, safeguard the interests of their members and the industry, reflect members' proposals on foreign trade to relevant government departments, and carry out activities to promote foreign trade.

Article 66 The State shall establish and improve a diversified dispute resolution mechanism for foreign trade, providing fair, efficient, and convenient avenues for foreign trade operators to resolve disputes through mediation, arbitration, litigation, and other means.

Article 67 China International Trade Promotion organizations shall, in accordance with their articles of association, conduct foreign exchanges, hold exhibitions, provide information, consulting services, and other foreign trade promotion activities.

Article 68 The State shall support and promote small and medium-sized enterprises in conducting foreign trade, and provide facilitation in supervision, financing, foreign exchange settlement, and other aspects.
Article 69 The State shall support and promote national autonomous areas and economically underdeveloped regions in developing foreign trade.

Article 70 The State shall support and promote the building of a foreign trade talent team, cultivate various types of talents adapted to the needs of foreign trade development, and provide talent support for the high-quality development of foreign trade.

Article 71 Whoever, in violation of the provisions of Article 13 of this Law, imports or exports goods subject to state trading administration without authorization, the competent department of foreign trade of the State Council or other relevant departments of the State Council may impose a fine of not more than 500,000 yuan; if the circumstances are serious, they may, within three years from the date on which the administrative penalty decision takes effect, refuse to accept the application of the violator for engaging in the import and export of goods under state trading administration, or revoke the authorization already granted to it to engage in the import and export of other goods under state trading administration.

Article 72 Whoever, in violation of the provisions of the third paragraph of Article 17 of this Law, imports or exports technologies that are freely importable and exportable without going through the contract registration formalities, the competent department of foreign trade of the State Council shall order it to make corrections and give a warning; if it refuses to make corrections, a fine of not more than 50,000 yuan shall be imposed.

Article 73 Whoever imports or exports goods the import or export of which is prohibited, or imports or exports goods the import or export of which is restricted without permission, the Customs shall handle and impose penalties in accordance with the provisions of relevant laws and administrative regulations; if a crime is constituted, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law.
Whoever imports or exports technologies the import or export of which is prohibited, or imports or exports technologies the import or export of which is restricted without permission, or fails to implement the necessary measures as provided in Articles 18 and 19 of this Law, shall be handled and penalized in accordance with the provisions of relevant laws and administrative regulations; if no provisions are made in laws and administrative regulations, the competent department of foreign trade of the State Council shall order it to make corrections, confiscate the illegal gains, and if the illegal gains are 500,000 yuan or more, impose a fine of not less than one time but not more than five times the illegal gains; if there are no illegal gains or the illegal gains are less than 500,000 yuan, impose a fine of not more than 500,000 yuan; if a crime is constituted, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law.
From the date on which the administrative penalty decision provided in the preceding two paragraphs takes effect or the criminal penalty judgment takes effect, the competent department of foreign trade of the State Council or other relevant departments of the State Council may, within three years, refuse to accept the application for an import or export quota or license submitted by the violator, or prohibit the violator from engaging in relevant goods or technology import or export activities for a period of not less than one year but not more than three years.

Article 74 Whoever engages in international service trade that is prohibited, or engages in international service trade that is restricted without permission, or fails to implement the necessary measures as provided in Articles 29 and 30 of this Law, shall be handled and penalized in accordance with the provisions of relevant laws and administrative regulations; if no provisions are made in laws and administrative regulations, the competent department of foreign trade of the State Council shall order it to make corrections, confiscate the illegal gains, and if the illegal gains are 500,000 yuan or more, impose a fine of not less than one time but not more than five times the illegal gains; if there are no illegal gains or the illegal gains are less than 500,000 yuan, impose a fine of not more than 500,000 yuan; if a crime is constituted, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law.
The competent department of foreign trade of the State Council may prohibit the violator from engaging in relevant international service trade activities for a period of not less than one year but not more than three years from the date on which the administrative penalty decision provided in the preceding paragraph takes effect or the criminal penalty judgment takes effect.

Article 75 Whoever violates the provisions of Article 37 of this Law shall be penalized in accordance with the provisions of relevant laws and administrative regulations; if a crime is constituted, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law.
The competent department of foreign trade of the State Council may prohibit the violator from engaging in relevant foreign trade activities for a period of not less than one year but not more than three years from the date on which the administrative penalty decision provided in the preceding paragraph takes effect or the criminal penalty judgment takes effect.

Article 76 Whoever, in violation of the provisions of Article 40 of this Law, engages in foreign trade activities with relevant foreign individuals or organizations or provides support, assistance, or facilitation such as agency, freight forwarding, delivery, customs declaration, warehousing, and third-party trading platform services, shall be handled and penalized in accordance with the provisions of relevant laws, administrative regulations, and departmental rules; if no provisions are made in laws, administrative regulations, or departmental rules, the competent department of foreign trade of the State Council shall order it to make corrections, confiscate the illegal gains, and if the illegal gains are 500,000 yuan or more, impose a fine of not less than one time but not more than five times the illegal gains; if there are no illegal gains or the illegal gains are less than 500,000 yuan, impose a fine of not more than 500,000 yuan; if a crime is constituted, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law.
The competent department of foreign trade of the State Council may prohibit the violator from engaging in relevant foreign trade activities for a period of not less than one year but not more than five years from the date on which the administrative penalty decision provided in the preceding paragraph takes effect or the criminal penalty judgment takes effect.

Article 77 In accordance with the first paragraph of Article 40 and Articles 73 to 76 of this Law, a person who is prohibited from engaging in relevant foreign trade activities shall, during the prohibition period, the Customs shall not handle the relevant customs declaration and inspection procedures for import and export goods based on the relevant prohibition decision, and the People's Bank of China, foreign exchange administration departments, and financial institutions shall not handle the relevant settlement and sale of foreign exchange procedures, receipt and payment of foreign exchange, cross-border RMB settlement, and other fund receipt and payment procedures based on the relevant prohibition decision.

Article 78 Any staff member of a department responsible for foreign trade administration work in accordance with this Law who abuses their power, neglects their duties, engages in malpractices for personal gain, or divulges or illegally provides to others the state secrets, work secrets, trade secrets, personal privacy, or personal information known to them shall be given a sanction according to law; if a crime is constituted, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law.
Any staff member of a department responsible for foreign trade administration work in accordance with this Law who, taking advantage of their position, extorts property from others, or illegally accepts property from others and seeks benefits for them shall be given a sanction according to law; if a crime is constituted, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law.

Article 79 If a party to a foreign trade activity is dissatisfied with an administrative act taken by a department responsible for foreign trade administration work in accordance with this Law, it may apply for administrative reconsideration according to law or institute an administrative action with the People's Court.

Article 80 With respect to foreign trade administration related to dual-use items, military products, fissionable and fusionable materials or materials derived therefrom, and other goods, technologies, services, and other items related to the maintenance of national security and interests and the fulfillment of international obligations such as non-proliferation, as well as the administration of import and export of cultural products, if laws and administrative regulations provide otherwise, those provisions shall prevail.

Article 81 The State shall adopt flexible measures and grant preferential treatment and convenience to trade between border areas of the country and the border areas of adjacent countries, as well as to border residents' mutual trade. Specific measures shall be prescribed by the State Council or the relevant departments authorized by the State Council.
Article 82 This Law shall not apply to the separate customs territories of the People's Republic of China.
Article 83 This Law shall come into force as of March 1, 2026.
